name: @argszero/cordis-plugin-empty-response-retry
description: Makes an unattributed empty model attempt retryable, for the one seam that can tell. Discussion #8321: a `dsh-llm-pi-ai` route that relays an upstream empty response ends the turn, because `classifyPiAiError` has no rule matching the wording, so the text falls to the catch-all `PI_AI_ERROR`, and that is the one code `DEFAULT_RETRYABLE_CODES` does not carry (`EMPTY_RESPONSE`, `RATE_LIMIT`, `SERVER`, `TIMEOUT`, `TRANSPORT`) — `dsh-llm-retry` short-circuits on `!policy.retryableCodes.includes(failure.code)` and the step is never repeated, though the same adapter maps a locally detected zero-content completion to the retryable `EMPTY_RESPONSE`, so two paths that both mean "the model produced nothing" disagree. This plugin observes the public `llm/stream` waterfall — the one seam that sees an attempt and everything it produced — and rewrites that finish's `failure.code` to the by-value `EMPTY_RESPONSE` when the attempt ended in an unnamed error AND produced nothing at all; the retry executor then accepts the step on its own unchanged code gate. It is strictly narrower than the `retryableCodes: [..., PI_AI_ERROR]` workaround in the report, which widens every catch-all failure on a route: the two producers the adapter marks deliberately non-retryable (`pending`, `deferred` — a not-yet answer is not the safe repeat the principle is about) are excluded, as is any attempt that emitted a block, a token, or a Tool call, and any failure the adapter did name. Nothing buffered, nothing reordered, one boolean of state.
